text:
nisha: heads-up: we started seeing persistent PCIe AER resets on p5 nodes after the 6.4 kernel rollout in ap-southeast1. multiple hosts reporting repeated "AER: corrected error" followed by nv-host OOMs and GPU module unloads.

alex: can you paste a short dmesg snippet? which kernel exactly (6.4.x)?

nisha: here's a representative chunk from host p5-47 (truncated):

```
[  552.342112] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Multiple corr_err status detected
[  552.342115] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: First error: ID 00e8: service 00
[  552.342117] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  552.342118] nvidia: probe of 0000:3d:00.0 failed with error -110
[  552.342119] kernel: nvidia_uvm has been registered
[  552.342121] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (python) total-vm: 123456kB
```

sam: saw similar symptom in eu-west-canary last night — NCCL handshake timeouts started ~15m after kernel went live, GPUs became unreachable intermittently, operator pods restarted.

lee: quick checks: dkms status on affected hosts shows nvidia drivers built against older headers? run `dkms status` + `uname -r` before doing anything. there's a known ABI change in 6.4 that breaks some prebuilt modules if they're not rebuilt.

jordan: confirmed on p5-47: `uname -r` = 6.4.0-rc2-custom, `dkms status` lists nvidia/525.125.06, installed for multiple kernels but the 6.4 build failed (missing symbols).

maria: impact summary from capacity side: ap-southeast1 lost ~18% of GPU capacity in the pool over the last 2 hours due to host evacuations. autoscaler is thrashing — we provision fallback on-demand instances in other zones which is increasing spend. rough estimate +17% on short-term infra cost if this continues.

opsbot: ALERT: gpu-host-flap-ap-southeast1 — 24 hosts unhealthy, 6 pods evicted, average eviction latency 42s, escalation required.

alex: can we avoid full rollback? if it's just DKMS/rebuild, we could trigger a targeted rebuild and restart of nvidia modules on canary hosts, then roll. but if kernel ABI change requires driver update, we may need to pin kernels or roll kernels back.

lee: rebuilding via DKMS helped earlier in the canary where we recompiled against the new headers. command I ran: `dkms autoinstall -k 6.4.0-rc2-custom` then `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` — but note some hosts still logged AER before the module rebind.

jordan: caution: one host showed persistent PCIe link retrains even after a rebind. that looked like a firmware/PCIe lane negotiation issue on the NIC -> affected NVLINK traffic too.

nisha: timeline: rollout started 02:10Z, ap-southeast1 started 02:38Z, first alerts 03:05Z. Canary eu-west rolled fine. This looks region-specific — maybe different BIOS/firmware baseline on ap-southeast fleet.

maria: region constraint: we can't shift critical customer jobs out of ap-southeast without SLA implications. We may have to spin up compensated dedicated nodes in us-west for degraded workloads, but that's a manual placement change. Cost/ops tradeoff.

alex: immediate actions proposal:
- pause further 6.4 kernel rollouts to remaining fleets (deploy-bot, hold rollout)
- run DKMS autoinstall + module rebind on affected ap-southeast hosts (parallel, canary 5 hosts)
- collect `lspci -vvv` + firmware versions + BIOS for hosts that fail rebind
- if rebind doesn't stabilize, schedule a kernel image rollback for the worst-off hosts
- open an incident ticket and notify customers in ap-southeast with impacted SLAs.

deploy-bot: Rollout hold enacted by alex at 03:28Z for kernel image 6.4.0-rc2-custom.

sam: +1 on rebuild attempt. I'll script a safe DKMS rebuild that retries and rebinds only on nodes with failed builds. I'll start with 5 canary nodes in ap-southeast1-b.

lee: mitigation notes — disabling AER is NOT acceptable as a long-term fix; it hides PCIe errors and will corrupt GPU workloads. Also watch for `nvidia_uvm` OOM messages — they indicate driver panic rather than just link flaps.

maria: ops/finance note: if we need urgent cross-region burst capacity, pre-approve a short-term 48h budget buffer of +25% for ap-southeast failover. Need signoff from finance on that.

jordan: I'll collect the failing host bios/fw and open a vendor support ticket with the NIC and board vendor (likely a firmware-grounded regression).

nisha: creating incident: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0423 (added logs, dmesg, failed dkms artifacts). tagging oncall.

alex: thanks. oncall — please own the rebuild script and coordinate rollback if rebuilds don't stick. keep updates here every 30m. :thumbsup:

maria: posted internal customer advisory draft to #customer-notifs, requesting review.

opsbot: NOTE: escalation to eng-sre if >30 hosts fail after rebuild window (60m).

nisha: update 04:10Z — first 5 canaries: 3 stabilized after DKMS rebuild + rebind, 2 still showing AER retrains. moving those 2 to rollback plan.

alex: good progress. keep a tight blast radius, prioritize least-disruptive path. document exact dkms build logs for the postmortem.

sam: pushing script now: `./tools/rebuild-nvidia.sh --nodes list.txt --kernel 6.4.0-rc2-custom --retry 3` — will post results shortly.

jordan: vendor ticket opened: NVEDIA-BRDG-7241 — attached lspci/fw for affected hosts.

maria: finance approved temporary +25% buffer for cross-region failover.

nisha: will follow up with full postmortem once we stabilize. current priority: stop rollout, rebuild where possible, rollback where not.

alex: thanks everyone. keep short updates here.
